answer: Continuous Presence Sampling requires each identity to answer random challenges from a sensor co-located with hardware it claims, such as a camera watching a glacier exhibit over months. An operator cannot fake physical continuity across thousands of sites at once, so cloned identities fail when their claimed locations diverge. Each forged identity costs the attacker dedicated hardware plus sustained field maintenance, priced like saffron per site-month. Cross-checking against karst terrain maps catches relayed feeds, since real sensor drift is location-specific.
